model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (GAAP, not FTE). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported; FY0 = H1 2026 actual 5,410 (NII 3,943 + noninterest income 1,467, Q2 2026 10-Q) + H2 2026 at ~2,795/quarter (Q2 run-rate was 2,837 = NII 2,052 + fees 785; NIM guided low-320s bps in Q3 rising to mid/high-320s in Q4, fees normalising from a strong Q2). Cross-check: September 2026 guidance of ~34% total revenue growth on FY2025 8,166 (NII 5,991 + fees 2,175) = ~10,940 GAAP / ~11,000 FTE-basis. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027, the guidance year, one year from the valuation date as the engine's end-of-year discounting requires. The CSV `Revenue` column (FY2025 1,562) is the ASC-606 fee subset tagged by XBRL and is NOT bank revenue; every revenue figure here is NII + noninterest income from the companyfacts/10-Q tags.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,020.4m common shares outstanding at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding = us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding 2,020,414,826) PLUS ~26m dilutive awards/warrants (Q2 2026 diluted weighted average 2,048.3m vs ~2,022m basic) LESS an ESTIMATED ~10m shares repurchased in Q3 2026 (~$155m at ~$16, the run-rate implied by $309m in H1 against the >= $550m FY2026 programme) = ~2,036m fully diluted at the valuation date. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation ($95m H1 2026) is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; the buyback is a distribution of the FCFE the model capitalises, not a separate driver. The ~462m shares issued for Cadence (1 Feb 2026) and the Veritex consideration are in the base count. REFRESH from the Q3 2026 10-Q cover (due late Oct 2026).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. Huntington is a Fed/OCC-regulated bank holding company: long-term debt $18,738m and short-term borrowings $3,111m at 30 Jun 2026 and deposits $222,466m are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and due from banks $3,330m is held against that funding and is not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the ~10% CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only. Preferred stock ($2,881m liquidation value, ~$164m/yr of dividends) is a claim senior to common and is deducted at book in equity_bridge; the flows are therefore total net income (before preferred dividends), NOT net income to common, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = GAAP net income ~2,780 (H1 2026 actual 1,250 incl. ~$300m after-tax merger/notable items; H2 at ~763/quarter = (2,795 revenue - ~1,720 noninterest expense - ~150 provision) x (1 - 18%)) LESS capital retained ~800 (~4% organic RWA growth x ~$19.3bn tangible common equity, i.e. NPAT x g/ROTE on a merger-depressed FY2026 NPAT). Cross-check on distributions: FY2026 common dividends ~$1,265m ($0.62 x ~2,040m) + buybacks >= $550m = ~$1.8bn, i.e. ~65% of GAAP NI distributed with CET1 held at ~10.0%. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 2,482; FY2022 4,027; Q3 2024 -58) is loan/deposit/trading movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV FreeCashFlow column is NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back: H1 2026 $95m (Q2 2026 10-Q) -> ~$190m annualised on the enlarged post-Cadence headcount; FY2025 $113m (10-K), FY2024 $133m (CSV). ~1.7% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow. No separate net-share-settlement tax line is tagged; taxes withheld on vesting are immaterial relative to SBC.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income ($10.3bn gross, $6.0bn net in FY2025) IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $309m in H1 2026 ($150m Q1, $159m Q2); FY2026 programme >= $550m with management signalling larger FY2027 repurchases alongside the September guidance reset. FY2022-FY2025 repurchases were nil (CET1 rebuild after TCF and the 2023 regional-bank stress, then the Veritex/Cadence deals). The flat share count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge in the flows; buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover count, plus estimated Q3 2026 repurchases)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Shareholders' equity $32,624m at 30 Jun 2026 less goodwill $9,527m, other intangibles (core deposit etc.) $915m and preferred stock $2,881m = tangible common equity ~$19,301m = ~$9.55/share on 2,020.4m (company-reported TBVPS $9.65, Q2 2026 release; the ~$0.10 gap is the company's deferred-tax adjustment on intangibles). AOCI -$2,213m is already inside equity. TCE ratio 7.1%, CET1 10.0% at Q2 2026 (management). Goodwill jumped from $5,997m to $9,527m on Cadence, so ROE on total equity (~11%) understates the ~17-18% earned on tangible common equity; the residual-income and FCFE arithmetic both work on the tangible base.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year US Treasury ~4.5% (late September 2026, after the Fed's first hike since 2023) + beta 1.2 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = 10.5%. Beta 1.2 is the measured five-year range (1.1-1.3) for a US super-regional bank and is above the 1.0 used for NAB.AX because US regional deposits proved flight-prone in March 2023 and HBAN's earnings are more NIM-geared than a big-four Australian bank's. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, integration and deposit-cost risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branch network, ~1,400 branches) are immaterial relative to $32.6bn of equity; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests. Preferred stock is the only senior equity claim and is deducted at liquidation value in equity_bridge (see funding_note), so the 18.0% cash-tax-rate driver is pure income tax (FY2025 effective 17.1%; H1 2026 18.2%; Q2 2026 18.4%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (house precedent NAB.AX 2026-09-24, IAG.AX, GL). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROTE)), and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. BVPS-compounding is NOT used: HBAN's GAAP book value is one-third goodwill after Cadence and swings with AOCI, so it is neither the earning base nor a usable compounding base. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income (GAAP); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision for credit losses) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue (H1 2026 actual: 5,410 - 3,583 - 290 = 1,537 = 28.4% + 1.7% SBC = 30.1%, depressed by ~$400m pre-tax merger costs and full-quarter Cadence expenses; FY2025 pre-merger: 8,166 - 5,015 - 481 = 2,670 = 32.7%); sbc_pct_path = 1.7%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation, software and core-deposit-intangible amortisation are inside noninterest expense and are genuine costs for a bank, not add-backs); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the ~10% CET1 target = NPAT margin x organic growth / return on tangible equity; cash_tax_rate_path = 18.0% income tax; wacc = cost of equity 10.5%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = -2,881 preferred stock. FY2027 base reconciliation: 11,000 x 1.055 = 11,605 revenue x (40.1% - 1.7%) x (1 - 18%) = 3,654 GAAP net income, less ~164 preferred dividends = 3,490 to common / 2,036m = ~$1.71 GAAP EPS, i.e. the bottom of the September 2026 guidance range of $1.75-1.83 (which excludes notable items; ~$50-100m of residual integration cost and $0.02-0.03 of CDI amortisation sit between the two). Base ROTCE ~17.8% GAAP on ~$19.6bn TCE vs the 18-19% adjusted 2027 target. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(CoE - g) = (17.8 - 2.5)/(10.5 - 2.5) = 1.91x x $9.55 = ~$18.3/share, which the engine base should approximate; the market's 1.60x TBV (8.9x guided FY2027 EPS) implies either ROTCE ~15.3% at a 10.5% cost of equity or a ~12.1% cost of equity at the guided ROTCE. Price is the NASDAQ regular close on 28 Sep 2026, not an after-hours print. Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) is unreported; 30 Jun 2026 is the latest balance sheet. Q2 2026 10-Q facts were read directly from the inline XBRL (EDGAR accession 0000049196-26-000066) because the companyfacts API had not ingested the filing on 2026-09-29.

equity_bridge.note: us-gaap:PreferredStockValue $2,881m at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q); dividends ~$164m/yr (H1 2026 $82m). Deducted at book because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (already after share-based compensation): FY2020 817 (COVID CECL build); FY2021 1,295 (TCF merger costs); FY2022 2,238; FY2023 1,951; FY2024 1,940; FY2025 2,211 (SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss, restated values from the latest 10-K). The 5-year CAGR (22.0%) measures recovery from the FY2020 provisioning trough plus the TCF acquisition; the 3-year CAGR (-0.4%) is from the FY2022 NIM peak. Revenue = NII + noninterest income: FY2015 2,990; FY2020 4,815; FY2022 7,254; FY2025 8,166 (5-year 11.1% is TCF-inflated; underlying organic ~4-5%). Diluted EPS FY2020 0.69, FY2022 1.45, FY2025 1.39.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (5.5% FY27 tapering to 2.5%), anchored on the 3-year revenue CAGR (4.0%) which is the only organic window: FY2020-21 includes TCF, FY2025-26 includes Veritex and Cadence. Equity CAGRs (11-13%) are acquisition share issuance, not retained earnings.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3/5-year CAGRs (11.1%/13.4%) diverge >30% from revenue (4.0% 3-yr) and EPS (-1.4% 3-yr): book value grew through stock-funded acquisitions (TCF 2021 +$6bn, Veritex/Cadence 2025-26 +$8bn incl. $3.5bn of goodwill) and AOCI swings, not through compounding, so equity CAGR does not describe per-share earnings power. EPS 3-year is negative because FY2022 was the NIM peak and 2023-24 carried deposit repricing; the 5-year 15.0% is from the FY2020 trough. Growth is taken from the revenue series and the FY2027 guidance.

base.growth_rationale: Total revenue. FY27 5.5%: no further full-year M&A effect (Cadence closed 1 Feb 2026, Veritex Q4 2025/Q1 2026), so this is organic: average loans +4-5% (guided 36-37% FY26 is acquisition-driven; underlying mid-single-digit in Texas/Southeast plus SBA/vehicle finance), exit-2026 NIM in the mid/high-320s vs ~3.20% FY26 average (+2-3% NII), fees +5-6% (payments, wealth, capital markets). Tapers to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP less structural deposit-beta creep), bracketing the 4.0% 3-year revenue CAGR.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue. FY27 40.1% = 100 - GAAP efficiency 56.1% (guided adjusted mid/low-54% by Q4 2026 + 1.8% core-deposit-intangible amortisation ~$215m + ~0.3% residual integration cost) - provision 5.5% (~30bp NCO on ~$195bn loans + reserve build for growth; H1 2026 ran 290 = 5.4%) + SBC 1.7. Mature 40.5% = efficiency 55.0% (CDI amortisation fading, synergies fully run-rate, offset by technology/compliance inflation) - provision 6.0% (mid-cycle ~33bp; FY2025 was 481/8,166 = 5.9%) + 1.7. FY2025 pre-merger actual was 32.7% pre-SBC on a 61% GAAP efficiency ratio, so the path assumes the Cadence cost synergies management has guided actually land.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~10% as RWA grows = NPAT margin (31.5-31.8% of revenue) x organic balance-sheet growth / ROTE ~16.3% (total NI incl. preferred over TCE + preferred ~$22.2bn) = ~1.95 x g. FY27-28 at 4.5% RWA growth: 8.8% of revenue (~$1.0bn, 28% of NPAT retained -> 72% distributed = $0.62 dividend ~$1.26bn + ~$1.4bn buybacks, consistent with management flagging larger FY2027 repurchases). Steps down with growth to 4.9% at the 2.5% terminal rate (~15% retained -> 85% distributed). Cross-check on CET1: 4.5% RWA growth on ~$21bn of CET1 capital needs ~$0.95bn.

bull.growth_rationale: Texas and Southeast commercial franchises grow loans 7-8% with deposit share gains, NIM holds ~3.30% as the Fed pauses after one hike and deposit betas stabilise, fees compound 8% on payments/wealth/capital markets cross-sell into the Cadence base. Revenue grows 7% FY27 fading to 3% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 54.5% GAAP (adjusted ~52.7% as synergies exceed plan) - provision 5.5% + 1.7 = 41.7. Positive operating leverage takes GAAP efficiency to 52.5% by FY30 with credit benign at ~5.0% of revenue (~27bp): 100 - 52.5 - 5.0 + 1.7 = 44.2, held. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$1.82 (top of guidance), ~$2.05 FY28.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~34.9% x g / ROTE ~19.5% = ~1.79 x g: higher growth needs more capital even at a better return. FY27-28 at 6% RWA growth retains 10.7% of revenue (~31% of NPAT); terminal 3% growth retains 5.4% (~15%).

bear.growth_rationale: The September 2026 cut is the first of several: the Fed keeps hiking, deposit betas rise faster than asset yields and NIM compresses to ~3.05% (the FY2024 level) while loan growth stalls at 1-2% as pricing tightens and integration distracts. Revenue flat-to-up 1% FY27-28, then 2-2.5% nominal.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 58.2% (revenue shortfall against a fixed cost base, integration overruns, CDI amortisation) - provision 8.5% (~48bp: office CRE, the newly acquired Texas/Southeast commercial book seasoning, consumer/vehicle normalisation) + 1.7 = 35.0. FY28 credit cycle: provision 11.0% (~62bp; FY2020 was 1,037 = 21.5% of revenue, so this is a mid-sized cycle, not a crisis) with efficiency 58.2%: 32.5. Recovers to provision 8.0% (~45bp) and efficiency 58.0%: 35.7, held - synergies partly offset by remediation and compliance spend; no operating leverage. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$1.41, FY28 ~$1.30; ROTCE ~12-13%.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~27.9% x g / ROTE ~12% = ~2.3 x g; FY27-29 held at 5.5% despite 0.5-2% growth because RWA migration and reserve build in a downturn consume capital the model must top up (CET1 at 10.0% and TCE at 7.1% leave little buffer; the 2023 precedent was a buyback halt for three years, not a raise). Terminal 2% growth retains 4.6%.

scenario_narratives.base: Huntington digests Cadence and Veritex, lands the guided cost synergies (adjusted efficiency in the low-54s by Q4 2026), and compounds revenue at 4-5% fading to 2.5% as Texas and Southeast commercial banking grow faster than the mature Midwest core. Provisions normalise to ~33bp mid-cycle. GAAP EPS reaches ~$1.71 in FY2027 (the bottom of the cut $1.75-1.83 guidance, ex-notables) and ~$2.20 by FY2031; 72-85% of earnings are distributed. At a 10.5% cost of equity and a ~17.8% return on tangible common equity the franchise is worth ~1.9x tangible book against the ~1.6x the market pays after the September sell-off.
scenario_narratives.bull: Integration runs ahead of plan, positive operating leverage takes efficiency to ~52.5%, the Fed pauses after one hike so NIM holds ~3.30%, and the Texas/Southeast franchises grow loans 7-8% with credit benign. FY2027 EPS hits the top of guidance and FY2028 clears $2.00; ROTCE ~19-20% matches management's target and repurchases scale up. The market's 8.9x forward multiple re-rates toward the 11-12x regional-bank norm.
scenario_narratives.bear: The September cut is the first of several. Deposit costs keep rising under a hiking Fed, NIM compresses toward 3.05%, loan growth stalls at 1-2% as pricing tightens, and a mid-sized credit cycle (office CRE, the freshly acquired and less-seasoned Texas/Southeast commercial book, vehicle finance) pushes provisions to ~60bp in FY2028. Synergies are partly eaten by remediation and compliance spend, efficiency stays near 58%, ROTCE settles at ~12% (barely above the cost of equity) and the buyback is halted to rebuild a 10.0% CET1 with a 7.1% TCE ratio. EPS falls to ~$1.30 before recovering slowly.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: management cut FY2027 EPS and FY2026 NII guidance within two months of reaffirming them, the Fed has resumed hiking (deposit-beta risk for a NIM-geared regional), two large acquisitions closed within months of each other on a loan book up 42% YoY, and CET1 10.0% / TCE 7.1% leave a thin buffer against a credit cycle. Bull cut to 25%: it needs synergies, benign credit, a Fed pause and a multiple re-rating all to hold, and the base already credits the guided cost-out.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regional bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity - never on statutory operating cash flow (which is loan and deposit movement) and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. GAAP net income is the flow; capital retention at NPAT x g/ROTE is the reinvestment; preferred stock is deducted at book so the common claim is valued; 10.5% is the return an owner requires from a NIM-geared US super-regional after March 2023. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a ~17.8% GAAP return on tangible common equity and 2.5% growth the franchise is worth ~1.9x tangible book, so the ~1.6x the market pays after the September 2026 guidance cut embeds either a ROTCE in the low-to-mid 15s or a cost of equity above 12%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$255bn of average earning assets is ~$130m of NII (~1.1% of revenue, ~3.5% of NPAT); the September 2026 cut was a ~5-8bp NIM revision and further Fed hikes push deposit betas the same way
Credit cycle: every 10bp on the provision rate over ~$195bn of loans is ~$195m pre-tax (~5% of NPAT); the acquired Texas/Southeast commercial and CRE books are less seasoned than the Midwest core
Integration: the base assumes the guided low-54% adjusted efficiency ratio lands by Q4 2026; every 1pp of efficiency is ~$115m pre-tax (~2.6% of NPAT)
Share count: the ~10m Q3 2026 repurchase estimate and the ~26m dilutive-award count are approximations until the Q3 10-Q cover prints; each 20m shares is ~1% of value per share

Capital: CET1 10.0% and TCE 7.1% leave little room; a Basel III endgame re-proposal, a Category III designation as assets approach $300bn, or a credit cycle could force retention above the modelled g/ROTE

Preferred stock is deducted at $2,881m liquidation value; if any series is redeemed at par with common-funded capital the value transfer is neutral, but a higher-coupon replacement would raise the ~$164m/yr leakage

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NASDAQ regular close); 52-week range 14.89-19.46.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000049196) for FY2015-FY2025 annual NII, noninterest income, net income, diluted EPS, equity, goodwill, intangibles, preferred stock, dividends and share counts; Q2 2026 10-Q inline XBRL (accession 0000049196-26-000066, filed 2026-07-28) read directly for the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, Q2/H1 2026 income statement, share-based compensation, repurchases, diluted shares and cover-page share count; HBAN_Metrics.csv / HBAN.duckdb (97 periods) for the reported history and kpis (buybacks, cash taxes). The CSV Revenue column is the ASC-606 fee subset and was not used.
data_sources.qualitative: HBAN_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): Cadence (Feb 2026) and Veritex acquisitions, Q2 2026 results (TBVPS, CET1, TCE, adjusted EPS), September 2026 Barclays-conference guidance cut (FY2027 EPS $1.75-1.83 from >$1.90; FY2026 NII growth ~35% from 39-43%), FY2027 ROTCE 18-19% and Q4 2026 efficiency targets, competitive position, CRE and rate risks, bull/bear cases.
